captions.text: One A-record edit. One client connects, the other cannot.
Same domain, same minute, two different results.
Step one: resolve the name. Step two: connect to the address.
Resolution succeeded. It returned the wrong destination.
Authoritative: .20 (wrong). Resolver A: .10, cached before the edit.
Resolver B asked after the edit and cached .20 for 60 seconds.
Client B still fails. The fix changed nothing for a full cache.
Cached at t=15 with TTL 60: expires at t=75, whatever you change now.
Expiry permits a new lookup. It pushes nothing.
t=60: resolver A refreshes on its next query.
t=75: resolver B's bad entry lapses; the next query fetches .10.
Resolver A recovered at t=60, resolver B at t=75. No single propagation time.
Not modelled: browser and OS caches, serve-stale, prefetch, AAAA.
Fixing the source does not erase every cached answer.
Record TTL is not content-cache lifetime. Separate clocks.
